title_prefix: A bitcoin.conf in the datadir shadowed b
mechanism: START-NODE-FROM-ARGS resolves exactly one config file and never asks whether a second one exists. src/node/init.lisp:1615-1624 sets CONF-PATH to the -conf value when the command line carries one, else <cli-datadir>/bitcoin.conf, and :1625-1629 reads that single file (or nothing, if it is absent). The effective datadir is a DIFFERENT quantity: "datadir" is an ordinary DEFINE-OPTION row (src/config-options.lisp:51, :key :data-directory), so a datadir= line inside the file that was read wins over the path used to LOCATE it and reaches START-NODE at src/node/init.lisp:1698-1701. Nothing between those two points compares the two, and a grep of src/ for Core's wording ("ignored, because", "which is ignored", "allowignoredconf") returns only the core-only row at src/config-options.lisp:435. Core at d3056bc does the comparison explicitly: common::InitConfig records orig_config_path = AbsPathForConfigVal(args, GetPathArg("-conf", BITCOIN_CONF_FILENAME), net_specific=false) BEFORE ReadConfigFiles (common/init.cpp:34-35, and the comment at :25-33 states that a config-file datadir= is honoured and that the second file it points at is ignored), then after the datadir is resolved checks fs::exists(base_path / BITCOIN_CONF_FILENAME) and !fs::equivalent(orig_config_path, base_config_path) and returns ConfigError{ConfigStatus::FAILED, ...} naming both files and the source of the override (common/init.cpp:65-95). GetBoolArg("-allowignoredconf", false) is the only way to downgrade it to LogWarning. Two adjacent halves of the same seam are also missing: our -conf value is used verbatim, while Core resolves a relative -conf against the base datadir (common/config.cpp:226-232), and Core makes an explicitly-set -conf that cannot be opened fatal ("specified config file ... could not be opened", common/config.cpp:139-142) where we fall through to no config at all.
consequence: The operator's entire second configuration file is dropped with no error and no log line, and the node runs on defaults for everything that file held. Both of Core's shadowing shapes reproduce, and in the -conf shape the prune target vanishes: dirC/bitcoin.conf carried prune=550 and rpcport=33333, and with -conf pointing elsewhere the node resolved :PRUNE NIL -- an unpruned sync on a disk that was sized for a pruned one, which is a disk-exhaustion outcome, plus rpcauth/rpcpassword, bind and txindex from the same file. Core refuses to start in exactly this situation, and states that it does so because the failure is otherwise invisible. -allowignoredconf compounds it: an operator who sets it is told the option has no effect, which reads as "this node has no such check" only if the startup log is read. Not S1: no chain data is destroyed and no consensus rule changes -- the node comes up on the wrong settings, which is the S2 shape (a durability/disk-space consequence from a config that silently did something else).
evidence: Executed in the project container (worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-options-s2b, warm image, probe build/ga11v/probe1.lisp: P1-RUN stubs the FDEFINITION of BITCOIN-LISP::START-NODE, captures the plist START-NODE-FROM-ARGS would have applied, and returns BL::*DEFERRED-LOG-LINES*). Fixtures: dirA/bitcoin.conf = {chain=regtest, datadir=/workspace/build/ga11v/dirB, prune=1000, [regtest] rpcport=11111}; dirB/bitcoin.conf = {chain=regtest, prune=2000, [regtest] rpcport=22222}; dirC/bitcoin.conf = {chain=regtest, prune=550, [regtest] rpcport=33333}; alt.conf = {chain=regtest, [regtest] rpcport=44444}. (a) conf-set datadir: args ("-conf=/workspace/build/ga11v/dirA/bitcoin.conf") -> :DATA-DIRECTORY "/workspace/build/ga11v/dirB/" :RPC-PORT 11111 :PRUNE 1000 :RESULT :STUBBED, logs = only (:INFO "Reading config file .../dirA/bitcoin.conf") plus the arg log; dirB/bitcoin.conf's 2000/22222 never appear and nothing warns. Core: base_config_path dirB/bitcoin.conf exists and is not equivalent to orig_config_path dirA/bitcoin.conf -> ConfigStatus::FAILED. (b) -conf shadowing the datadir file: args ("-datadir=/workspace/build/ga11v/dirC" "-conf=/workspace/build/ga11v/alt.conf") -> :DATA-DIRECTORY "/workspace/build/ga11v/dirC/" :RPC-PORT 44444 :PRUNE NIL :RESULT :STUBBED, no warning; dirC/bitcoin.conf's prune=550 is gone. Core: FAILED with the "Data directory ... contains a bitcoin.conf file which is ignored, because a different configuration file ... from command line argument \"-conf=...\" is being used instead" text. (c) -allowignoredconf=1 added to (b): :RESULT :STUBBED and the only warning is (:WARN "Accepted but NOT implemented by this node, so this option has no effect: -allowignoredconf") -- the dimension-wide mitigation fires for the flag but never for the condition, which needs no option at all. (d) adjacent, same seam: ("-datadir=.../dirC" "-conf=bitcoin.conf") reads NO file (no "Reading config file" line, :RPC-PORT NIL :PRUNE NIL) where Core would resolve it to dirC/bitcoin.conf; ("-datadir=.../dirC" "-conf=.../nope.conf") also starts silently with no config where Core is fatal. Sources: src/node/init.lisp:1615-1629, :1698-1701; src/config-options.lisp:51, :435; src/node/datadir.lisp:65-83 (%CHECK-DATADIR-OPTION -- the OTHER half of Core's InitConfig, the "specified data directory ... does not exist" check, IS present and fired in a control run against a missing -datadir, so the absence here is specific to the shadowed-conf check and not a missing InitConfig); refs/bitcoin/src/common/init.cpp:20-35, :65-95; refs/bitcoin/src/common/config.cpp:122-142, :226-232; refs/bitcoin/src/init.cpp:508.
fix_shape: Port Core's InitConfig ordering into START-NODE-FROM-ARGS. Record two paths before the merge: the datadir as the command line and defaults give it (orig_datadir_path) and the config path actually read, resolved the way Core resolves it -- absolute as given, relative joined onto the BASE datadir, empty under -noconf (AbsPathForConfigVal, common/config.cpp:226-232). Make an explicitly-set -conf that cannot be opened a fatal CONFIG-PARSE-ERROR with Core's "specified config file ... could not be opened." wording, which closes the relative-path and typo cases at the same time. Then, after the merged config has settled the effective datadir, if <effective-datadir>/bitcoin.conf exists and does not resolve to the file that was read, signal a fatal error carrying Core's full text (both paths, the config_source clause distinguishing "data directory" from "command line argument -conf=", and the three remedies including "Set allowignoredconf=1"), and downgrade it to LOG-WARN only when -allowignoredconf is true -- which means moving "allowignoredconf" out of DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS into a real DEFINE-OPTION row so it is both readable and no longer reported as having no effect, and adding it to the known-config-options set in the same commit. Under -noconf, emit Core's LogInfo instead of the error (common/init.cpp:70-74). Tests: one case per shape (-conf shadowing, conf-set datadir=, -noconf, allowignoredconf=1 downgrade, relative -conf resolved against the datadir), each asserting the effective value of a setting that lives only in the shadowed file so a passing test cannot be satisfied by the error text alone.
